transcript.text: I need to flag an engineering constraint before we proceed. This morning, while debugging an unrelated queue-consumer issue, I discovered that more than 2 concurrent inference requests can exhaust the triage worker's connection pool. When that happens, timeouts bypass the intended manual-review fallback and leave tickets without a routing label. I haven't filed this in the launch ticket yet. The good news is that capping concurrency at 2 in the rollout configuration is sufficient to satisfy this engineering constraint — no separate engineering deployment is needed before flag enablement.

transcript.text: I need to raise a customer operations constraint. During a recent customer-account review for another queue change, I confirmed that six accounts — AsterBank, Northstar Health, LumaPay, GreenField Benefits, Harbor Mutual, and Vantage Clinics — have contractual clauses prohibiting automated ticket decisions until they receive 72 hours' prior notice and retain human review. None of these accounts has been notified yet about the AI ticket-triage rollout, and I have not added this notification requirement to the launch checklist. This is a customer operations constraint that needs to be addressed before we can proceed with the flag enablement next Tuesday.

At a 10% cohort that projects to $14,400 per month. To keep costs within budget, the initial cohort must be exactly 5% and a cost alert must trigger at exactly $8,000 monthly spend. I confirmed these numbers minutes ago but have not yet updated the rollout proposal.
